status: PROTOTYPE - every value under fits is a placeholder until models/fit-coupons-v1 and this prototype's fit strip are printed and judged

ring.source: 28 pins / 27 lobes = Codex workbook example; radius and pin size chosen by the author for the wrist drum (78 mm); 4 x 28 dowel (26 -> 28 with the 1.0 disc gap - MP6 L4 R1 F4)

disc.axial_gap_note: disc 1 above the motor screw heads and disc 1 to disc 2; 1.0 makes the cam spacer 2.0 thick (min material) and leaves 0.4 above the screw heads even if the lower cam slides the whole gauge height down to the pilot (MP6 L4 R1 F1 / F4)
disc.note: the second disc is the same part turned 180 deg about its own centre - with 27 (odd) lobes this is NOT the same outline, it is the half-lobe shift the opposite eccentric needs

bearings.status: proposal - the user buys; d x D x B are the series' nominal values, not checked against a data sheet here. ASSUMPTION ring sections: d + min_factor (D - d) <= inner-ring outside diameter <= d + factor (D - d) and D - factor (D - d) <= outer-ring bore <= D - min_factor (D - d) - a shoulder must stay clear of the other ring using the wide bound (factor) and must overlap its own ring inside the band every ring surely has (min_factor)

motor.status: MEASURED 2026-11-04 by the user (motor ledger src/cad/calibration/motor-mks42d.json · MP14): shaft_dia 5 · shaft_flat_to_axis 2.0 (4.5 across the flat) · pilot_dia 22 · pilot_height 2 · shaft_length 21.5 (19.5 above the pilot) - the length of the D flat along the shaft is NOT measured (both cams are D bores: the flat must run 18.9 from the tip). ASSUMPTION - bolt_square · frame · screw_thread_depth = NEMA17 common values; screw head = M3 button head (ISO 7380 class) nominal, not checked against a data sheet; screw_thread_depth = usable thread depth in the motor flange

cam.note: lobe = 6801 bore, journal = 6800 bore (both + fits.bearing_bore_extra); shoulder_dia = hub and spacer between the 6801 inner rings (touches inner rings only); the lower cam is a press fit on the D shaft set by the gauge, the upper cam a slip fit (fits.cam_upper_bore_extra) resting on the 6801 #1 inner ring

washer.note: between the second 6801 inner ring and the 6800 inner ring (both input speed); the printed variants let the user take up the axial stack tolerance

gauge.note: removable fork: sets the lower cam this far above the motor pilot while it is pressed on the D shaft of the motor alone (before the motor goes on the base); 0.6 = three 0.20 layers

carrier.note: shoulder_dia = collar under and flange over the 6808 inner ring; the 6800 seat has a relief above the inner ring so only the outer ring meets the carrier

housing.note: outer_ring_shoulder_dia = cap lip under and retainer over the 6808 outer ring (touches the outer ring only)

fits_from.note: printer / material fit values (pin holes, bearing seats and shafts, D bores, pilot, M3, inserts) live only in the ledger - cycloid.load_params() fills them into fits; never write them here

fits.status: design clearances only (author choices). The calibrated values come from the ledger (fits_from): bearing_seat_extra adds to every printed bore that takes a bearing outer ring (6801 / 6800 / 6808); bearing_bore_extra adds to every printed shaft that takes a bearing inner ring (lobes, journal, carrier hub) - judged as a hand push fit (slides in by hand without play), never pressed: pressing an inner ring onto a lobe or the journal would push the lower cam down; pin_press_hole_dia = base holes (pins pressed), pin_slip_hole_dia = cap holes (the cap slides over the pins); d_bore_extra adds to both cam D bores (diameter, flat moves by half), cam_upper_bore_extra adds on top for the upper cam's slip fit

fit_strip.note: test pieces - the strip's 1.0 floor under the pin holes and the 0.6 gauge are thinner than min_material on purpose (not part of C3)
